newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves through customer RP's.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves through customer RP's.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to add temporary reserves to the banking system on Wednesday via customer repurchase agreements, analysts said.
Market watchers said, however, they do not rule out the possibility of more aggressive action by the Fed.
"With fed funds trading just above target, we acknowledge the risk of more aggressive (Fed move)," said Dana Saporta, economist at Stone & McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
Saporta said with Wednesday being the final day of the central bank's current two-week liquidity maintanence period, "it makes the Fed call even more uncertain."
Kevin Flanagan, economist at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc, said he expects the Fed to add reserves more aggressively. "We are leaning in the air of an overnight system," he said.
Analysts said the Fed's daily average add need is perceived to be between $4.0 and $5.0 billion in the next maintenance period which begins on Thursday.
